summary: Re-reviewed earlier: MC std / Cramer-Rao ratio 0.875-1.106 for the 3 identifiable cells, systematic pattern as stated, scope correctly limited to self-consistency (shared model/table), not physical fidelity. No overclaim.

Reviewed earlier: statistic correctly scoped as iodine line integral g/cm2 on 27 rays, 2-material estimator on 3-material phantom; 1e6/1e5 bias ratios M2 0.89, M4 1.02 consistent with dose-independence; framed as implementation confirmation, not discovery.

Re-ran verify2.py on real 48 P2 rays, noise-free MLE, all converged. M2 signed-mean z: iodine tilt +10% = +4.6, -10% = -5.2 (rms/floor 0.82/0.92); iodine escale +-2% z -22.3/+23.1 (rms/floor 3.79/3.94); WATER tilt z -23.6/+25.1 (rms/floor 3.99/4.26). Matches claims. Not over-corrected: iodine tilt bias is only 0.66-0.75 floor per ray and z~5 arises only by pooling 48 rays; z assumes a pure-noise null (20 draws/ray, no other bias source) and is a noise-free hypothetical power, not an observed statistic. Suggested wording changes: (a) say iodine-tilt case is marginal (z~5 only via pooling, not per-ray); (b) my M4 P2 recompute with the same rms/floor definition gives 27-43x (signed z 186-294), not 21-38x; conclusion unaffected but correct the range or state its definition.

Re-ran: full-rank fraction at rtol 1e-2 = 0% (M2 k=2), 58.33% (M4 k=2 P2), 0% (M4 k=3 P3); 100% for 1e-3..1e-10. sv_min/max 0.0020-0.0066 (M2), 0.0048-0.0123 (M4 k2), 0.0022-0.0094 (M4 k3), consistent with 0.0020-0.0123. Median iodine CRLB k=2 P2 1e6: M4 0.00151, M2 0.00376 (ratio 2.49x), exact. Not overstated: labelled idealised upper bound (no detector response/charge sharing/pile-up); structural vs empirical separation correct. Not re-run by me: condition numbers (195/99/217) and the 2.4x rms figure.

RECOMPUTED from model_data npy: mu matrix, col angle 1.043deg, SVs 3.697/1.176/0.0029, cond 1272.9 all reproduce. BUT it is the zero-thickness (spectrum-mean) matrix. Beam-hardened local effective mu (-dlnT/dP) at 10cm: cond 912-964, angle 0.94-0.97deg; at 25cm: cond ~754-796, 0.87-0.91deg; calcification column drops 25-40%. So cond=1273 is an upper bound; 750-1270 realistic; order of magnitude survives. MORE SERIOUS: 'exact recovery in noiseless challenge data is possible' is FALSE in image domain. Downloaded the real kit (md5 7aaf6b55 OK): real lowkVp/highkVp images deviate from linear model A@x by ~0.026/0.016 per cm (~10%) on tissue; repo's sum_to_one inversion on real kit cases 0-2 gives RMSE 1.56 vs zero-prediction 0.446; tissue-only RMSE 1.70-1.78 vs 0.567. A 5-10% mu mismatch is amplified (sigma_max(B^-1[:,:2])=343) into garbage. Fix: scope claim to exact-linear synthetic; state mismatch result.

Downloaded real kit and checked ALL 10 cases. Case-0 numbers reproduce under strict defs (exact0 35.14%, |s-1|<=4e-8 59.5%, strictly between 5.35%). Split is IDENTICAL in all 10 cases (support mask identical; allclose sums) so no variation - but this means 10 samples are one geometry, not independent evidence. Threshold-dependent: at |s-1|<=1e-3 it is 36.3/60.4/3.4. No fourth class: true (sum<=1.0000, never >1.001, no negatives). ERROR: text says maxima 'calcification 0.566 (10-case sample)' - 0.566 is case 0 only; 10-case max is 0.738 (per-case 0.566-0.738). Band deficit median 0.58, 10% quantile 0.006: band is heterogeneous.

Synthetic only (labelled). Recomputed sigma_max(B^-1[:,:2])=343.4; 343.4*|b|(0.3724)/|x|(0.7071)=180.9 matches 181. Comparing 181 to cond=1273 (0.14x) is apples to oranges but harmless. Caution: inherits F-012 exact-linear-model assumption; on real images mismatch dominates (see F-012).

Band fraction '~5%' is case-0 strict-threshold (5.35%); 3.4% at 1e-3 tol (all 10 cases). Claim that band error >> deficit is synthetic-only and not labelled so; on real kit images the TISSUE pixels fail (tissue RMSE 1.7 sum_to_one) because of model mismatch, so 'boundary pixels are the hard case' does not transfer. AIR_CUTOFF caveat honestly stated.

Numbers match metrics.json: s1 sum_to_one 1.1788, zero_prediction 0.4301, simplex 0.0508, boundary_rmse 3.838; unconstrained 0.3027. Synthetic caveat stated. But band is 1650/17408=9.5% of synthetic pixels vs 3.4-5.4% real. REAL-DATA CHECK (kit cases 0-2, repo code, RMSE): zero 0.446, unconstrained 0.317, sum_to_one 1.555, simplex 0.379. So sum_to_one worse than nothing holds on real data, but simplex does NOT clearly beat zero (0.379 vs 0.446, worse than unconstrained) and cause is model mismatch not the band. 'Regime-separated reporting mandatory' fine; the 'simplex wins' ordering is a synthetic-generator artifact.

Overclaim: 'whole-tree git_dirty flag is ALWAYS true' - RUN-0006 record shows git dirty=False (RUN-0003 True). Process claim; could not replay runmeta. Reword to 'was true in RUN-0003/4/5 because outputs were tracked'.

Recomputed with real polychromatic model: truth [8,4,.05] -> decoy [12.7219,-0.5106,0.1], lnT residual 1.3e-15, ||dx||=6.53 reproduces. But that decoy has negative fibroglandular, unreachable for any constrained method. Searched nonneg decoys (grid of truths, total<=16 cm): largest FULLY NONNEGATIVE ||dx||=19.7 cm (truth [1,14,0.2] -> [15.27,0.37,0.35], resid<1e-10), so claim is STRENGTHENED, the negative example is just poorly chosen. Caveats: per-ray result; map-level exactness unproven (null direction rotates 0.02-0.05deg with path, so pixelwise-constant shift leaves lnT residual ~1e-4 or worse); 'network converges to whichever prior prefers' is extrapolation.

(a) 'Larger decoys do go negative, so nonnegativity bounds the family' is wrong: fully nonnegative exact decoys exist with ||dx||=19.7 cm (truth [1,14,0.2]->[15.27,0.37,0.35]) vs the 0.26 band example. Band decoy [0.735,0.073,0.006] reproduced (resid 2.5e-16, sum 0.814). (b) sum-to-one removing pixelwise ambiguity holds only in the linear exact model, but real images are ~10% off linear (F-012) so paper identifiability does not give recoverability. (c) real fractions 36.3/60.4/3.4% (1e-3) vs claimed 35/60/5.

Fetched arXiv 2604.25356 PDF: 'soft tissue and calcification were chosen as basis materials'; 'two input and output channels'; MBIR with lambda=0 unregularized; loss is MSE of LE/HE projections (Eq.5/6); text says median while Table 1 caption says Mean RMSE (inconsistency flagged by lead). 2-from-2 confirmed. Not rechecked: 5.83 vs 13.07, Sec 4.2 inverse-crime wording.

Fetched arXiv 2311.10641: discriminator learns from 'reference low-noise material-specific images' generated 'from SECT using threshold and normalization', 'do not have to be associated with the input DECT'; reference not ground truth but same threshold method used for eval GT. Confirms unpaired-reference, not label-free. Not checked: lambda, SD -91-97%, square 2x2 ROI-derived A.

Tried: recomputed every arm's 3-seed mean s1 and proj RMSE from results.json (RUN-0047-49,64-72,74-79,83-85,88-90); applied the rule under 3 readings of 'pooled range' (range of 6 values, mean of ranges, max range): no arm qualifies under any. All quoted numbers reproduce. Problems: (1) 'no ... improves' overstates a non-rejection: the rule has no stated detection floor; with occ_softmax range 0.26 it triggers only for mean s1 < ~0.02. Say 'none shown to improve'. (2) 'The sum direction was never the limitation' is UNSUPPORTED and arguably contradicted: the soft-partition arms failed their manipulation check - tissue |S-1| 0.035-0.080 (w=1.6e-5) and 0.042-0.043 (w=1.6e-4 seeds 1-2) vs softplus baseline 0.034-0.051, air |S| unchanged (~4e-5) - so the sum was never constrained; softmax3/oracle are confounded by saturation (F-042). The only sum-pinned, non-saturated run (RUN-0066, |S-1| 0.0056) is the single success, and within occ_softmax s1 orders with |S-1| and proj RMSE. With S pinned and calc~0 the swap is data-visible (independent CRB ~0.025/ray at 6 cm, see F-043 review). Delete the sentence or replace with 'the partition arms did not change |S-1|, so whether pinning the sum helps is untested'.

Tried: s1 0.09142 matches results.json and diag.json; per-case 0.079-0.106, 100/100 <0.15; Pearson 0.970, 83% within 0.1, bimodal histogram all reproduce from diag.json. Checked selection uses val projection loss only (milestone_a.py:244). Problems: (1) 'the projection loss did not select it' compares proj RMSE ACROSS parameterisations (unlike with like): softplus seeds reach lower residual because their sum is free and they slide along the exact null. WITHIN occ_softmax, proj RMSE ranks the 3 seeds exactly as s1 (1.11e-3/1.75e-3/7.7e-3 vs 0.091/0.282/0.351) - n=3, weak, but the opposite of the headline. (2) 1.2e-3 is the 12-case diag value; the 100-case value is 1.11e-3. (3) 'No evaluation artifact found': the recompute reuses metrics.s1_mean_rmse; only the per-case formula is independent - say so. (4) A data-driven explanation is available and should be listed: RUN-0066 has S~0.994 and calc~1e-4, i.e. near the sum+calc-known regime where the swap is visible (sensitivity ~0.038/cm vs 3e-3 with calc unknown). Reword title to 'not ranked best by projection RMSE across arms; ranked best within its arm'.

Tried: re-read diag script (exp024_anomaly_diag.py:52,58-66,129-142) and diag.json; independent single-ray polychromatic calculation on kit tables (scratchpad ident.py). Errors: (1) The probe n is the 3-decimal F-012 vector (milestone_a.py:35), 0.024 deg from the exact zero-thickness null; M@n_rounded = (-6.8e-4,-4.1e-4)/cm, M@n_exact ~1e-15. At t=0.1 per ray the transmission change is 3-8e-5 for n_rounded vs 0.02-1e-5 for n_exact (L=2-12 cm): most (~85-97%) of the reported 3e-4/unit-t slope is rounding residual (mostly through the -0.008 calc component), not curvature of the loss along the null family. Real (beam-hardening) curvature is 5-30x smaller. (2) '~100x below' is overstated as stated: nets carry null-coordinate error RMS ~0.6, giving ~1.8e-4 RMSE on the probe vs residual 5.5e-4..1.2e-3 (3-6x); the corrected, smaller real curvature restores a large gap, but for a different reason. (3) cos(n,(-1,1,0)/sqrt2) = 0.9997, not ~0.97. (4) 'conditioning ~1e3' (F-012/F-025) is the partition-constrained number and does not apply to the unconstrained physics-only arms. (5) 'Truth is its exact minimiser' (1.3e-8) reflects the inverse-crime identity of generator and forward (EXP-017); it shows nothing about strict minimality along the exact null. 'null_dir_error_frac uninformative' is justified (even more strongly). Also RMSE range omits softmax3 (0.33). Rerun the profile with the exact SVD null (float64) before keeping any number.

Tried: read grad_norm in every history.json at thresholds 0/1e-12/1e-8/1e-6; inspected pred()/oracle path (milestone_a.py:47-50, 193, 208-220) and diag saturation code; no bug found in the oracle (truth S used only as the control intends). Errors: (1) 'exactly 0' holds for RUN-0083/85/67/68 (first exact zero steps 100/99/123/113) but NOT RUN-0084 (plateau ~7e-12, <1e-8 from step 133) nor RUN-0088 (median 5.6e-11, <1e-8 from step 261, not ~96). Say '<1e-8 (exactly 0 in 4 of 6)'. (2) RUN-0084 is one-hot but NOT constant (75:25 spatial mix, std 0.433, Pearson ~0). (3) lr evidence: seed 0 at lr 3e-5 dies at step 261 vs 96 - both after a similar cumulative warm-up Adam step (~3.4e-3 vs ~4.7e-3 per parameter) and the train loss falls 50x (8.8e-3 to 1.7e-4) during collapse. So collapse is loss-decreasing descent into a vertex that lower lr delays but does not prevent; 'saturation causes the collapse' is nearly tautological (collapsed = saturated) and the driver is not isolated (candidate: uniform-softmax init puts 1/3 calcification, whose suppression inflates logit scale). (4) RUN-0090 has 57% of steps <1e-6 grad norm; 'live' depends on the 1e-8 threshold (Adam eps 1e-8). Final 'supports neither identifiable nor not' is correct.

Tried: independent numpy re-derivation from the raw kit .npy (scratchpad ident.py, own binning and photon bookkeeping). Reproduced: sum(0.5*spectrum)=1 so T(0)=1; DECT reduced sv 3.4567/3.057e-3; CRB 0.249 (DECT), 0.155/0.131/0.124/0.120 (PCCT 2/4/8/32); DECT/PCCT-32 ratio 1.92-2.18 over all 9 (L,comp) cases; photon convention (DECT N/2 per kVp, PCCT bins share one N) correct; profile CRB with nuisance correct. Problems: (1) The CRB treats calcification as an unknown nuisance: the weak partition direction is a/f swap traded against ~1% calc. With calc known absent AND sum known, DECT CRB is 0.041/0.025/0.029 (L=2/6/12, 50/50) - 10x better - and PCCT-32 gives NO gain (0.046/0.027/0.029). With calc known but sum unknown: DECT 0.20, PCCT 0.10. So 'PCCT at most ~2x' and '0.249' hold only in the calc-unknown model; state this in title/statement. (2) PCCT 'rank 3' is NOT structural: smallest/largest sv 4e-5..1e-4 vs threshold 1e-6 (numerical; no K-edge, near-2-basis physics). (3) Assumptions to state: equal incident photons (not dose), PCCT uses the 80 kVp spectrum only, single ray. (4) Curve angle 2.45-2.67 deg is a different quantity from F-012's 1.04 deg; say so.

R2 delta review (RUN-0091 diag.json). Numbers reproduce: M@n=(-1.4e-15,-2.2e-16); null profile 4.03e-6 @0.1, 1.61e-5 @0.4 (linear, symmetric); swap 1.31e-3/1.34e-3 @+-0.1 (5.09e-3/5.55e-3 @+-0.4, mildly asymmetric); ratio 326x; cos 0.99972. WRONG: (1) 'differs only by ~0.8-1% calcification': n - 0.9997*swap = (-0.0157,-0.0157,-0.0078), i.e. calc -0.78% AND total A+F -3.1% (sum change -0.039/unit t). Using kit M: calc-only compensation leaves 5.4% of swap visibility, sum-only 12%, n with calc zeroed 70%; both compensators are needed (2 measurements need 2 DOF) for the exact null. Say 'compensated jointly by calcification (-0.008) and total-tissue (-0.031) change'. (2) 'calcification (or sum) freedom hides the error' in trained solutions is CONTRADICTED by the same file: tissue calc means are 0 to 1.8e-3 (mostly <1e-4) while null/swap coordinates are |t|~0.1-1.0 (mean -0.42..+0.99, std 0.15-0.70); following n would need calc ~0.008|t| and negative calc for t>0 (infeasible under calc>=0 where truth calc=0). Trained errors are NOT along n; with cos 0.9997 'null_coord_t' is a swap coordinate. Their residuals (5.5e-4..1.3e-2, 4-6 orders above the 1.3e-8 floor) are visible, not hidden; ray-integration cancellation of spatially varying t(x) and sum freedom are the candidate reasons the residuals are smaller than a uniform swap of the same pixel RMS. (3) 'flat along n to 3 digits' is arithmetic (adding <=1.6e-5 in quadrature to >=5.5e-4), not evidence; RUN-0047 is ~0.9% non-flat and monotone. (4) 'swap |t|=0.05 exceeds best residuals' compares a uniform global swap to spatially varying errors; ray averaging makes it a best-case floor. Also: n is the zero-thickness null; linear RMSE is the first-order beam-hardening residual (correctly noted).

R2 delta review, independent script (scratchpad crb.py, own loader of data/aapm_kit_sample tables, Poisson Fisher on counts, 1 unknown a with P=(aL,(1-a)L,0)). Calc=0 and sum known, 2e5 incident photons: 6 cm 50/50 SECT-50 0.0220, SECT-80 0.0302, DECT(1e5+1e5) 0.0252, PCCT-4 0.0277, PCCT-32 0.0270; DECT range over 2/6/12 cm x 0.2/0.5/0.8 = 0.024-0.041, matches. Calc-free nuisance, sum known DECT 0.246 (vs 0.249). Scope caveats that must stay: (a) depends on exact knowledge of sum (chord L) and calc=0 - one nuisance DOF of calcification raises it 10x; (b) exact forward model (CRB is variance only; F-025 model mismatch is bias amplified by the same conditioning); also the AAPM data are noiseless, so 2e5 photons is a hypothetical regime and per-ray (ray-average) not per-pixel. Wording: EXP-034/S3 'identical to 2 digits at 2 and 12 cm' is false at 2 cm (SECT-80 0.053, DECT 0.041, PCCT-32 0.046, SECT-50 0.035); 'spectral bins add nothing' holds. The calc-known numbers are not in the RUN-0087 record; bind them to a run before promotion.

R2 wording only: title says 'the projection loss did not select it' but the corrected statement says selection is unresolved (within-arm ranking matches s1). Change title to '...; whether the projection loss selects it is unresolved'.

R2 wording only: title 'saturate ... and lose all gradient within ~100 steps' overgeneralises - RUN-0088 ~261 steps, RUN-0089/90 (oracle) keep live gradients. Title should say 'in 6 of 8 softmax3/oracle runs' or similar.
